images.caption: The U.S. Navy destroyer tender USS Prairie (AD-15) with destroyers at San Diego, California (USA), in August 1962. The ships alongside are USS Shields (DD-596), USS Agerholm (DD-826), USS Richard B. Anderson (DD-786), and USS Evans (DE-1023).

images.caption: A U.S. Navy UGM-109 Tomamhawk cruise missile hits (and sinks) the target ship, the decommissioned Gearing-class destroyer USS Agerholm (DD-826), off Point Mugu, California (USA). The Tomahawk was launched from a distance of ca. 320 km from the nuclear-powered attack submarine USS Guitarro (SSN-665).
images.alt: A U.S. Navy UGM-109 Tomamhawk cruise missile hits (and sinks) the target ship, the decommissioned Gearing-class destroyer USS Agerholm (DD-826), off Point Mugu, California (USA). The Tomahawk was launched from a distance of ca. 320 km from the nuclear-powered attack submarine USS Guitarro (SSN-665).

images.filename: Mothballed cruisers at Mare Island Naval Shipyard on 12 July 1960.jpg
images.caption: Vertical view of  of Berths 21 through 24 of the U.S. Mare Island Naval Shipyard, California (USA), looking northwest, 12 July 1960, showing Pacific Reserve Fleet and other ships. Those present include (from top): Two Cleveland-class light cruisers, USS Roanoke (CL-145), USS Worcester (CL-144), another Cleveland-class light cruiser, USS Lyman K. Swenson (DD-729) undergoing FRAM II modernization, two auxiliaries and USS Agerholm (DD-826) receiving FRAM I modernization. One of the Cleveland-class cruisers is USS Vicksburg (CL-86).
images.alt: Vertical view of  of Berths 21 through 24 of the U.S. Mare Island Naval Shipyard, California (USA), looking northwest, 12 July 1960, showing Pacific Reserve Fleet and other ships.
